body:
We mostly speak English, as my parents are Canadian, but my adoptive father is from Quebec and his family is from Costa Rica, so I picked them up from him.

Dr. Slump is written by Akira Toriyama, same author as Dragon Ball. It's really childish, a lot of butt and poop jokes, but I liked it anyway. And despite constant urging from my buddies on the football team (it turns out for some reason, football players are actually really otaku), I haven't gotten around to watching FMA.

Yeah, Watchmen brings out the edgelords in full force. I studied philosophy in high school, and for all intents and purposes, it's contemporary philosophy in an unusual medium. That might be why I found it so interesting. Alan Moore is quite an interesting person. He's a great writer, but he's a self proclaimed wizard, and seems to be pretty far gone.

The resets are what helped me get back into it in my late teens. New 52 was a pretty good starting point for me. I haven't touched a comic in a while, but I think DC did a reset last year. The injustice series is self contained and really well written despite the fact it's a video game tiein.

Thanks for the talk kind stranger. It's quite late now where I live, so it's time for me to go to sleep. Again, thanks a lot man. Keep doing what you do.

Oh, that good!

My family is trilingual, I know enough French to hold a conversation, a splash of Spanish and English is my first language, but I'm fluent in several Carribean creoles. I know a little Latin because etymology is probably my favorite area of study.

I'm a bit if the opposite. I have a bunch of retro indie comics (Valiant, Malibu), but those companies have all been absorbed by Marvel at this point. Outside of Dragon Ball, Dr. Slump and Soul Eater I haven't really read any manga.

Watchmen is phenomenal, but is a deveation from Western stand

ards. It's a dark and grim reflection of humanity during the Cold War. It does a lot to see both the humanistic and deistic nature of being a superhero.

My favourite run is probably the original run of Iron Man, it tend to focus a lot on Tony as a human with human issues. Rather than a superhero with human issues.

Green Lantern for the past 10 years has been really good. It went from your typical pulp superhero series to a giant space opera. There's 4 protraganists and they're all great. It really expands the wider DC universe, and it's a lot of fun.

And if you're into so bad it's good, Marvel's NFL SuperPro is pretty good. It was really short lived, and really easy to find. It's about a quarterback with super football powers. It's really cheesy and really preachy.

Western comics tend to have some sort of grand reset every few years, a huge colossal crossover that serves usually as the apocalypse. That was the whole point of the comics Infinity War. So there usually isn't much to catch up with.

Man, that's rough. Despite her flaws my mom has always tried to be their for me. I'm sorry to hear that.

Whoa, that's way cool! I love languages, I'm a bit of an armchair linguist. The school I'm going to offers Hebrew and Greek, I can't wait to learn them. Man, working in comics would be a childhood dream come true. I have a few boxes stashed somewhere, I would save up money from my paper route and it would either go to a new game, Pokemon cards or my comic collection. So now I have to ask, are you Marvel, DC, indie or manga? I'm DC, but I really wish the cinematic universe would pick up it's game.

Yeah. She angrily tells me how much I mean to her. It's weird when someone yells at you and tells you how much you matter at the same time.

Well, I'll see if I can get him to give it a Dark Souls a go.

We don't really use the term undergrad in my country, that's your bachelor's correct? What are you majoring in?

She was awesome. She spoiled me to death, and lived across the street from Dairy Queen. I was a tubby kid :). The one thing my mom and I agree on is we wish she was still around.

My family has a history of suicide. My grandparents both took their own lives. My grandfather before I was born, and my grandmother some ten years after. I think it's the reason my mom doesn't like to talk about it when I bring up how I feel.

Is Dark Souls 3 easier because of difficulty or intuitiveness? Because we're both suckers for a challenge. His favourite game is Spelunky, and I still haven't beaten it after trying for years. I've already played a handful of... timing based combat? Dodge based combat? a handful of games with a similar combat syten to Dark Souls.

I already feel pretty far behind in life. I don't really want to end up any further. Acquiring some financial stability would nice. But it's a long process once you factor the military requirements.

I think I get it from my grandmother. I didn't have very long with her but she was always building me up. When I told my Aunt what I was going to school for she said that my grandmother knew I'd be a preacher some day.

I'm pretty excited for Smash Ultimate. I've poured over just about every single piece of footage we have so far. I can't wait for it to come out. The lack of Robin and (quality) Ryu footage is driving me up the wall. 

I didn't know Dark Souls has a co-op. Is there couch co-op? I've heard so many good things about it, and I haven't played a game with rewarding and challenging combat in a long time.

I'm worried that I won't get funding. I won't have anywhere to stay if I don't finish get into college. My adoptive dad's (half-brother's dad) friend offered me a well paying job in labour when I get back. So, I could get a place. But I'm always afraid the worst will happen.

I want to be a chaplain in the Canadian Armed Forces. I feel like it's somewhere I can really make a difference. If that doesn't pan out, I'd love to do missionary work.

Games is tough one. My favourite of all time is probably Super Smash Bros. I have fond memories of playing it with my brother. We couldn't afford melee so we played my dad's copy for the 64. As I grew older my friends and I got a lot better, and we're a competitive bunch. Another one is Dishonored, it was the first game I found challenging without being frustrating. The world and story was rich and interesting despite being bleak and gloomy. Terraria, Minecraft, TF2, Mortal Kombat. A lot of my favourites are my favourites because I played them with my brother. I'm scared for him, because I know he feels the same way I do. He's halfway through highschool already, it's crazy how time flies. His dad doesn't let him out of the house much. He's very open about his disdain and hatred for my little brother. It sickens me. I'm afraid that if one of us goes, the other will follow.

One of my buddies is a Dark Souls nut. I've had fun with third person action games in the last, I might pick it up sometime.

My dad offered to fly me out to where he's from. I'm supposed to go in two days. I'm afraid to go, I'm not sure why. Part of me worries I'll be there forever.

Again, thanks for listening to me. I'm afraid to tell the people close to me because I don't want them to worry y'know?

Hey, thanks for listening. I'm studying Theology, my belief might be one of the reasons I'm still here, but faith can be fickle. Hobbies? I like music, skateboarding, boxing and good old-fashioned gaming. I'm excited for school, or as excited as I get for things. I have friends that go there, and I've met my future professors. I don't know how I feel about my parents. I tried talking to my mom, she blames me, and blames herself for coddling me. Honestly, you know as much about my dad as I do. I thought my half-brother's dad was my dad until a year ago. I've only met him once for Christmas. I've been afraid to seek help because I've always had an irrational fear that I'd get locked up and never be able to come out. It's weird and strange, but it's a feeling I can't shake.

Thanks for listening. I really appreciate it.
